metadata.title: Commander Succession Database -- Union and Confederate
metadata.purpose: Records all command changes during the battle with approximate tick numbers for the animation engine to update displayed commander names in unit info panels.
sources: OR Vol. 27, Parts I and II
Busey, John W. and Martin, David G. -- Regimental Strengths and Losses at Gettysburg (1994)
Hessler, James A. and Motts, Wayne E. -- Pickett's Charge at Gettysburg (Savas Beatie, 2015)

union_successions.event: Reynolds KIA -- Doubleday assumes corps command
union_successions.cause: KIA
union_successions.notes: Reynolds shot through the head at the edge of Herbst Woods while directing the Iron Brigade. First general officer killed at Gettysburg.

union_successions.event: Doubleday replaced by Newton -- Meade sent Newton to replace him
union_successions.cause: Meade's order -- loss of confidence in Doubleday
union_successions.notes: Meade had lost confidence in Doubleday. Newton transferred from VI Corps to command I Corps. Doubleday was deeply offended and spent years defending his actions.

union_successions.event: Meredith wounded -- Robinson assumes Iron Brigade
union_successions.cause: Wounded -- concussion from horse falling on him under fire

union_successions.event: Paul blinded -- Leonard assumes brigade (1st succession)
union_successions.cause: Wounded -- shot through both eyes, blinded permanently

union_successions.event: Leonard wounded -- Root assumes brigade (2nd succession)
union_successions.cause: Wounded

union_successions.event: Root wounded -- Coulter assumes brigade (3rd succession, 4th commander)
union_successions.cause: Wounded
union_successions.notes: Four brigade commanders in under an hour -- a remarkable succession.

union_successions.event: Stone wounded -- Wister assumes Bucktail Brigade
union_successions.cause: Wounded
Wounded

union_successions.event: Hancock wounded -- Hays assumes corps command
union_successions.cause: Severely wounded -- nail and saddle pommel fragments drove into thigh
union_successions.notes: Hancock refused to leave the field until Pickett's Charge was fully repulsed. He was carried off still issuing orders.

union_successions.cause: Wounded during Pickett's Charge
KIA -- shot through abdomen in the Wheatfield
union_successions.notes: Hancock told Cross before the charge 'This is not your last battle, Colonel.' Cross reportedly replied 'I think this IS my last battle, General.'

union_successions.cause: KIA -- mortally wounded in the Wheatfield
Multiple wounds during the charge
KIA
KIA -- killed by artillery shell

union_successions.event: Sherrill mortally wounded -- Bull assumes brigade
union_successions.cause: Mortally wounded during Pickett's Charge
Right leg amputated -- artillery shell
union_successions.notes: Sickles was carried off smoking a cigar to show his men he was not dying.

union_successions.cause: KIA -- shot through head on horseback leading countercharge

union_successions.event: Graham wounded and captured -- Tippin assumes brigade
union_successions.cause: Wounded and captured in Peach Orchard collapse

union_successions.event: Vincent mortally wounded -- Rice assumes brigade
union_successions.cause: Mortally wounded on Little Round Top -- died July 7
KIA on Little Round Top summit
Severely wounded at Barlow's Knoll -- left for dead
union_successions.notes: Gordon gave Barlow water believing him dying. Both survived and became friends after the war.

union_successions.cause: KIA -- shot through mouth while serving last gun at The Angle
union_successions.notes: Cushing received the Medal of Honor posthumously in 2014 -- the longest gap between action and award in MOH history.

union_successions.cause: KIA on Little Round Top summit -- killed beside the dying Weed
KIA leading Colgrove's controversial charge
union_successions.notes: Mudge reportedly said 'It is murder but it is the order' before leading his men forward.

confederate_successions.cause: Left arm shattered by artillery fragment
confederate_successions.notes: Hood's arm was permanently paralyzed. He continued to serve but never recovered full use of it.

confederate_successions.event: Law to division -- Sheffield assumes brigade
Barksdale mortally wounded -- Humphreys assumes brigade
confederate_successions.cause: Mortally wounded leading the Peach Orchard charge -- died July 3
confederate_successions.notes: Barksdale was riding ahead of his men when shot. Found by Union soldiers, he died in a Union field hospital.

confederate_successions.event: Semmes mortally wounded -- Bryan assumes brigade

confederate_successions.cause: KIA on horseback at The Angle
confederate_successions.notes: Garnett rode because he was too sick to walk. His body was never conclusively identified after the battle.

confederate_successions.event: Kemper severely wounded -- Mayo assumes brigade
confederate_successions.cause: Shot through groin -- briefly captured, survived

confederate_successions.event: Armistead mortally wounded beyond The Angle
confederate_successions.to_commander: No successor -- Armistead falls among Union troops
confederate_successions.cause: Shot moments after breaching The Angle -- died July 5
confederate_successions.notes: Armistead fell among Union soldiers beyond the wall. He asked for Hancock to be brought to him. He died July 5 in a Union field hospital.

confederate_successions.cause: Head wound -- folded paper in hat cushioned the blow
confederate_successions.notes: Heth survived. The folded paper in his oversized hat -- the hat did not fit well -- almost certainly saved his life.

confederate_successions.event: Pettigrew to division -- Marshall assumes brigade

confederate_successions.cause: KIA leading brigade in the charge
Captured -- first Confederate general taken since Lee assumed command
confederate_successions.notes: When Union soldiers recognized Archer, one reportedly said 'Good morning, General -- we are glad to see you.' Archer was furious. He died in captivity in 1864.

confederate_successions.event: Pender mortally wounded -- Lane then Trimble commands
confederate_successions.to_commander: Major General Isaac Trimble (for July 3 charge)
confederate_successions.notes: Pender was one of Lee's most promising division commanders. His death was a serious blow.

confederate_successions.event: Avery mortally wounded -- Godwin assumes brigade
confederate_successions.cause: Shot through neck on Cemetery Hill slope -- wrote blood message dying
confederate_successions.notes: Avery dipped his finger in the blood from his wound and wrote: 'Tell my father I died with my face to the enemy.'

confederate_successions.cause: Stuart rejoins army after controversial absence
confederate_successions.notes: Lee reportedly greeted Stuart with 'General Stuart, where have you been?' Stuart had been absent since late June on his controversial ride around the Union army.

confederate_successions.event: Hampton wounded -- Fitz Lee senior present
confederate_successions.cause: Sabre cut to head in East Cavalry Field melee
